source.title: Bi-LoRA: Efficient Sharpness-Aware Minimization for Fine-Tuning Large-Scale Models
source.authors: Yu-Hang Liu; Tao Li; Zhehao Huang; Zuopeng Yang; Xiao-Lin Huang

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: Compares a different sharpness intervention and loss-landscape measurement with held-out performance, but does not test the catalog versions’ specified settings or measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports fine-tuning benchmark scores and loss-landscape and train–validation-gap results bearing on sharpness and generalization. Benchmark scores alone do not measure the train–test gap or test the specified versions. Cited prior findings are not extracted as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses sharpness minimization to develop a fine-tuning method and reports its performance and diagnostic landscapes. It does not test any listed version. For V7, filter-normalized random-direction loss plots on CoLA and train–validation curves on MRPC do not establish that magnitude-aware sharpness ranks generalization gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that Bi-LoRA improves fine-tuning generalization and full-parameter landscape flatness while avoiding SAM's additional gradient step; Appendix O reports a smaller MRPC train–validation gap.
record.recipe_differences: Fine-tuning pretrained models with low-rank adapters and an auxiliary adversarial adapter; compares Bi-LoRA with LoRA and LoRA-SAM. It does not use the original claim’s model families or specified interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, model, perturbation space, clipping scheme, auxiliary rank, and neighborhood radius are varied in the paper; no qualifying claim-version test is established.

fits_no_version.finding: On T5-base fine-tuning, LoRA-SAM is flattest within the adapter space, whereas Bi-LoRA improves full-space flatness more on CoLA. Separately, Bi-LoRA has a smaller train–validation gap on MRPC with similar training losses.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An auxiliary adversarial adapter can improve full-space perturbation tolerance and held-out fine-tuning performance relative to LoRA baselines.

record.problems: The reported landscape and train–validation-gap findings are figure-only, without numerical values in the text. The MRPC gap result is described qualitatively; the paper does not report the specific magnitude-aware sharpness measure required by V7.
record.rows_left_out: Benchmark task scores and efficiency measurements were not extracted: they compare fine-tuning methods but do not themselves measure the specified claim versions or train–test gap. Other qualitative sharpness and robustness plots were omitted because the retained rows capture the stated landscape and generalization-gap findings.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting, natural-label held-out accuracy, and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under the same training recipe.
Network widening beyond zero training error; adapter-rank sweeps do not establish this condition.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under limited or broader tuning.
Batch-size effects under matched epoch budgets and adaptations that recover performance.
Controlled dropout addition or removal and its dependence on data size or augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance before training error rises, its ranking of generalization gaps among comparably fitted networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus removing equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The qualitative row values are supported by the supplied text, although numerical figure values are unavailable. Their states are cannot_determine relative to the listed claim versions, not a rejection of the reported method improvements.

versions.untested_parts: Width sweep past interpolation and test error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD under the specified tuning regimes.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout addition and removal under the stated regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness perturbations and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: LoRA-SAM
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss-landscape flatness within LoRA and full parameter spaces.
rows.measure: Loss-landscape flatness under random filter-normalized directions.
rows.value: LoRA-SAM is flattest within the LoRA parameter space; in full parameter space it is flatter than LoRA, but loss still rises sharply with perturbation magnitude.
rows.note: Qualitative description in the text; precise plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The qualitative landscape description matches the text, but measures perturbation-induced loss rather than V7's magnitude-aware training-error tolerance and its relationship to generalization gaps. This is a method diagnostic.

rows.subject: Bi-LoRA
rows.operation_detail: Compared loss-landscape flatness within LoRA and full parameter spaces.
rows.measure: Loss-landscape flatness under random filter-normalized directions.
rows.value: Bi-LoRA delivers a substantially greater improvement in flatness in the full parameter space.
rows.note: Qualitative description in the text; precise plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: The text reports greater full-space flatness for Bi-LoRA, but this comparison of the proposed method with baselines does not measure V7's sharpness–gap ranking.

rows.subject: Bi-LoRA
rows.operation_detail: Tracked training and evaluation losses, accuracies, and generalization gap.
rows.measure: Training and evaluation losses and metrics; generalization gap.
rows.value: Training losses were nearly identical across methods; Bi-LoRA had lower validation loss, higher accuracy, and a smaller train–validation generalization gap.
rows.note: Text describes directions of results; plotted values are not stated.
rows.check: Appendix O supports the qualitative description of similar training losses and a smaller validation gap. No corresponding magnitude-aware sharpness measurement is reported on MRPC, so this method-performance result cannot establish V7.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
